assumptions_challenged: That a guidance document (MISEV2023) alone constitutes demonstration that SGL-001 meets orthogonal EV characterization and CMC requirements.
That source‑cell MCB/WCB generation and characterization for SGL‑001 have been completed and documented.
That validated, fit‑for‑purpose intact‑EV analytic methods for SGL‑001 (with LLOQ, specificity, precision, accuracy) are available.
That a stability‑indicating, mechanism‑linked potency assay correlated to an in vivo PD endpoint for SGL‑001 exists.
That reproducible GMP‑like batch release/stability/potency comparability for SGL‑001 has been demonstrated.
That rodent intranasal biodistribution data alone predict intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species without orthogonal intact‑EV readouts and bridging controls.
falsification_conditions: Provide MCB/WCB generation records and characterization reports for the source cell line(s) used to make SGL‑001.
Provide validated intact‑EV analytic method reports for SGL‑001 (particle counts, protein/lipid markers, EV‑specific markers) including validation metrics: LLOQ, specificity, precision, and accuracy.
Provide a validated, stability‑indicating potency assay for SGL‑001 and data demonstrating correlation of potency readout to an in vivo PD endpoint.
Provide representative release, stability, and potency comparability data across ≥3 GMP‑like batches showing predefined acceptance criteria and lot‑to‑lot consistency.
Provide formulation/device compatibility recovery data (ex vivo and in vivo controls) demonstrating intact‑EV recovery after processing and administration.
Provide cross‑species biodistribution data that include orthogonal intact‑EV readouts and demonstrate reproducible CNS exposure in a larger species relative to rodent controls.
strongest_objection: The supplied evidence is a consensus guidance (MISEV2023) that prescribes what must be demonstrated; it does not provide any program-specific empirical or validated manufacturing/analytic data for SGL-001. Therefore the claim that SGL-001 is sufficiently characterized (identity, potency, lot-to-lot comparability) or that rodent intranasal data predict intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species is unsupported by the provided evidence.
